questions.question_text: The current prevalence of heroin use in the UK is
questions.explanation: The current prevalence of heroin use in the UK is around 1% (male -to-female ratio of 2:1), with most treatment seekers being in their 20s.

questions.question_text: What percentage of patients taking benzodiazepines for nearly a year develop dependence syndrome?
questions.explanation: Rate of dependence varies with duration of use - 15% of those using 1 -5 months of prescribed benzodiazepines develop dependence compared to nearly 40% of those using it for nearly a year (De lasCuevas, 2003).

questions.question_text: How much of heroin does a typical heroin dependent user consume on a day?
questions.explanation: Illicit heroin is sold as a brown or white powder in 'bags' or 'wraps', costing £50 - £100 (median value £80 in the UK as of 2014) per gram, with a typical dependent user taking 0.25 - 2.0 g per day. It is most commonly consumed by smoking (chasing) but is also taken orally, occasionally snorted, and parenterally by IV, IM, or subcutaneous routes. Street supplies are of variable purity (25 -50% by volume); an occasional pure batch may be associated with a series of deaths and overdose due to higher potency.

questions.question_text: Ice is the street name for a particularly strong and pure form of
questions.explanation: Many synthetic forms of amphetamines are now available. Methamphetamine is a potent form that can be inhaled, smoked, or injected intravenously. Ice (crystal meth) is a particularly strong purer form - smoked or injected. Oral IV and snorting possible; called whiz or speed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an acute effect caused by LSD (Lysergic acid diethylamide)?
questions.explanation: Acute harmful effects of LSD include 'behaviours related to toxicity (i.e. harm related to acting on beliefs such as having the ability to fly) and 'bad trips' (i.e. dissociation, fear of incipient madness, frightening perceptions). There is no risk of overdose, and physiological dependence and withdrawals do not generally occur.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a preferred maintenance treatment after opioid detoxification?
questions.explanation: Buprenorphine is considered to be a safe option to treat opioid dependence with a very low potential for abuse, especially when used in combination with naloxone in a sublingual preparation (Suboxone).

questions.question_text: Suboxone is a drug that contains
questions.explanation: Suboxone contains buprenorphine as well as the opioid antagonist naloxone to deter the abuse of prescribed buprenorphine via intravenous injection of the crushed tablets.

questions.question_text: Which drug has no evidence base for treating opioid withdrawal symptoms?
questions.explanation: There is a substantial evidence base for three main types of pharmacotherapy: 1. Methadone 2. Buprenorphine and 3. α2 adrenergic agonists (e.g. clonidine and Lofexidine). All three groups of medications are shown to be effective in reducing withdrawal symptoms.

questions.question_text: Mr. Z is a gentleman with a history of using illicit drugs in the past. He is observed to have a nasal septal perforation. Which of the following is the most likely offending drug?
questions.explanation: Cocaine is an alkaloid derived from the shrub Erythroxylon coca. It is a powerful positive reinforcer - strong dependence producer. It is a potent dopamine reuptake blockade. It can be injected, smoked or snorted. It may cause nasal septal perforation due to local anaesthetic effect with repeated trauma, and vasoconstriction and ischemic necrosis.

questions.question_text: 'Crack' is a pure form of which of the following street drugs?
questions.explanation: Street cocaine can be freebased (released free from the base e.g. sodium bicarbonate which is mixed with it) to produce purer form called crack - acts as rapidly as IV when inhaled.

questions.question_text: Tolerance does not develop to one of the following features of opiate use
questions.explanation: While tolerance to nausea, vomiting, sedation, euphoria and respiratory depression occur rapidly, there is a minimal development of tolerance to constipation and miosis.

questions.question_text: The intervention with most consistent evidence base among all psychosocial interventions for cocaine users is
questions.explanation: Contingency management refers to interventions in which clients receive tangible, positive reinforcers for objective evidence of behaviour change. Patients may receive a voucher, exchangeable for retail goods and services, or a prize draw lottery whenever they submit a drug negative urine specimen.

questions.question_text: The common side effects of benzodiazepines include which of the following?
questions.explanation: The most common side effects of benzodiazepines are drowsiness and dizziness.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a specific benzodiazepine antagonist used in accident and emergency departments to reverse the effects of the benzodiazepines?
questions.explanation: Flumazenil is a specific benzodiazepine antagonist used in A&E/ICU to reverse the effects of the benzodiazepines.

questions.question_text: Which benzodiazepine has been particularly implicated in cases of 'date rape'?
questions.explanation: Flunitrazepam: A short-acting potent benzodiazepine used particularly in dance settings for intoxicant and weak aphrodisiac effects. It results in impaired judgement and anterograde amnesia.

questions.question_text: According to ICD10 diagnostic coding, which term is used to denote the state where alcohol causes actual physical or mental damage, but the drinker has no dependence pattern yet?
questions.explanation: ICD10 has a diagnostic code for 'harmful use' where actual damage is caused to the drinker physically or mentally, but he/she has no dependence pattern (yet).

questions.question_text: The most commonly used opioid in the UK is
questions.explanation: Heroin is the most commonly used opioid and it is most commonly smoked (called chasing) or injected IV/IM though it can be snorted or taken orally too.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is no longer used as patients developed prolonged QT intervals associated with fatal torsades de pointes?
questions.explanation: Levo-alpha-acetylmethadol (LAAM) is a long-acting derivative of methadone. It suppresses withdrawal for 48 to 72 hours and has the advantage of requiring less frequent clinic visits than methadone. It is no longer used as patients developed prolonged QT intervals associated with fatal torsades de pointes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an alpha -2 adrenergic agonist, licensed for the management of symptoms of opioid withdrawal?
questions.explanation: Lofexidine is an alpha-2 adrenergic agonist, licensed for the management of symptoms of opioid withdrawal. It can counteract the adrenergic hyperactivity associated with opioid withdrawal, demonstrated by characteristic signs and symptoms such as tachycardia, sweating, runny nose, shivering and goose bumps.

questions.question_text: Mr.Z has presented to A and E with a history of ingesting an illicit drug. He believes that he can fly. Which of the following could be the most likely offending drug?
questions.explanation: LSD: Acute harmful effects are behavioural toxicity (i.e. harm related to acting on beliefs such as having the ability to fly) and 'bad trips' (i.e. dissociation, fear of incipient madness, frightening perceptions).

questions.question_text: Which one among the following drugs is recommended by NICE guidance as the first choice treatment for opioid dependence?
questions.explanation: The 2007 NICE Guidance on the management of opioid dependence recommends oral methadone or buprenorphine as the preferred pharmacotherapeutic options for opioid dependence.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is due to the chronic harmful effect of cocaine?
questions.explanation: Acute harmful effects include arrhythmias, intense anxiety, hypertension, CVA, acute impulsivity, and impaired judgement. Chronic harmful effects include necrosis of nasal septum, foetal damage (crack babies), panic and anxiety disorders, persecutory delusions, and psychosis.

questions.question_text: The term cold turkey is commonly used to refer to
questions.explanation: The term cold turkey is often used to refer to opioid withdrawal state. Opioid withdrawal is rarely fatal in a healthy adult.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs and their street names are incorrectly matched?
questions.explanation: The street drug name 'crack' refers to the freebase cocaine.

questions.question_text: The common cause of death in benzodiazepine overdose is usually due to
questions.explanation: In contrast to barbiturates, the benzodiazepines have a larger margin of safety in overdoses. The ratio of lethal dose to effective dose is about 200 to 1 or higher.

questions.question_text: A pregnant woman who is currently using heroin wants to undergo opioid detoxification. Which of the following is the best period to undertake opioid detoxification in a pregnant woman?

options.text: Should not be attempted when pregnant
As soon as possible in any trimester

questions.explanation: Opioid detoxification is typically avoided in the first trimester due to an association of spontaneous abortion with withdrawal. It is also avoided during the third trimester due to the association with fetal stress and preterm labor.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a common side effect of clonidine?
questions.explanation: Clonidine causes excessive sleepiness.

questions.question_text: With respect to naltrexone use in opioid dependence, which of the following is true?

options.text: Dysphoria, depression and insomnia are not known side effects of naltrexone
The evidence for the use of naltrexone for relapse prevention in opioid users is inconclusive
It can be initiated irrespective of the amount of current opioid use
Naltrexone is superior to methadone in relapse prevention among opioid users
Naltrexone implants have better evidence base as adjuvants in relapse prevention

correct_answer.text: The evidence for the use of naltrexone for relapse prevention in opioid users is inconclusive

correct_answers.text: The evidence for the use of naltrexone for relapse prevention in opioid users is inconclusive

questions.explanation: Following successful withdrawal from opioids, naltrexone may be administered on a chronic basis to block any future effects of opioids. Naltrexone appears to have some limited benefit in helping formerly opioid-dependent individuals to remain abstinent, although the quality of the evidence is relatively poor and heterogeneous.

questions.question_text: In an average user, LSD can be detected in urine for up to

options.text: LSD cannot be detected in urine

questions.explanation: Since the half-life of LSD is only a few hours, only a very small amount of LSD remains even at the end of the trip, and this is excreted in the urine.

questions.question_text: The risk of seizures associated with bupropion use is estimated as
questions.explanation: The risk of seizures associated with the anti-smoking agent bupropion is 1 in 1000.

questions.question_text: Untreated heroin withdrawal symptoms typically reach their peak within how many hours after the last dose?
questions.explanation: Untreated heroin withdrawal symptoms typically reach their peak within 32-72 hours after the last dose and symptoms will have subsided substantially after five days.

questions.question_text: Mr. X has been consuming a high dose of cannabis for a long time. How long will it be present in his urine?
questions.explanation: Cannabis - (Urine drug screen) Occasional use - up to 3 days. High daily use for long time - up to 4 weeks.

questions.question_text: For cessation of smoking, nicotine replacement treatment should be used for a period of
questions.explanation: All nicotine replacement treatment should be used for about 8-12 weeks but may be continued beyond this time if needed to prevent relapse.

questions.question_text: Which class of drugs are commonly abused by athletes and bodybuilders seeking competitive advantage?
questions.explanation: Anabolic steroids: These prescription-only medicines (e.g. nandrolone and stanozolol) can be abused by athletes and bodybuilders seeking competitive advantage or, more rarely, for their euphoriant effects alone.

questions.question_text: Roid Rage is an acute emotional instability associated with the use of
questions.explanation: Use of anabolic steroids is associated with physical health problems including hypertension, hypogonadism, gynaecomastia, amenorrhoea, liver damage, impotence, and male pattern baldness; and with mental health problems including acute emotional instability (sometimes known as roid rage), increased aggressiveness, persecutory/grandiose delusions, depressive illness, and chronic fatigue.

questions.question_text: Kinaesthetic hallucinations are reported in cases with
questions.explanation: Symptoms of Benzodiazepine withdrawal include autonomic hyperactivity, increased tremor, insomnia, nausea or vomiting, transient visual, tactile, or auditory hallucinations or illusions, psychomotor agitation. anxiety (most prominent), with grand mal seizures and kinaesthetic hallucinations reported in a few patients.

questions.question_text: Which atypical antidepressant has been advocated by NICE for smoking cessation?
questions.explanation: Bupropion is an atypical antidepressant with dopaminergic and noradrenergic actions and has been advocated by NICE for smoking cessation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about caffeine is incorrect?

options.text: Caffeine acts as an antagonist of the adenosine receptors
Caffeine at high doses can affect dopamine and noradrenergic neurons
Caffeine does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier.
The half-life of caffeine in the human body is 3 - 10 hours

correct_answer.text: Caffeine does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier.

correct_answers.text: Caffeine does not readily cross the blood-brain barrier.

questions.explanation: Caffeine readily crosses the blood-brain barrier.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is associated with an amotivational syndrome?
questions.explanation: A controversial amotivational syndrome has been associated with long-term heavy use of cannabis.

questions.question_text: A 53-year-old gentleman has a long-standing history of illicit drug use and has been recently diagnosed with lung cancer. Which of the following agents is potentially associated with carcinoma of lung?
questions.explanation: Cannabis is normally smoked with tobacco. In addition, benzyprene, a carcinogen, is present in the tar of both tobacco and cannabis cigarettes.

questions.question_text: Flashback phenomenon is commonly reported after ingesting which of the following substances?
questions.explanation: Long after ingesting a hallucinogen like LSD, a person can experience a flashback of hallucinogenic symptoms.

questions.question_text: Mr. Z presented to the A and E with rashes around his nose and mouth and an unusual breath odour. On examination, he shows signs of ocular and oropharyngeal irritation. What class of substances on consumption produces this presentation?
questions.explanation: A recent inhalant user may have rashes around nose and mouth; unusual breath odours, the residue of the inhalant substances on body or clothes; and can show signs of ocular and oropharyngeal irritation.

questions.question_text: Smoking does not induce the metabolism of
questions.explanation: Lithium is renally cleared without undergoing any hepatic metabolism.

questions.question_text: Bad trip is the most common adverse effect of;
questions.explanation: Bad trip is the most common adverse effect of LSD and related substances.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs have shared amphetamine-like stimulant effect and LSD-like hallucinogen effect simultaneously?
questions.explanation: MDMA is a substituted amphetamine. It produces subjective effects resembling those of amphetamine and LSD (lysergic acid diethylamide).

questions.question_text: The drug that is not licensed in UK for smoking cessation is
questions.explanation: The three main treatments licensed in UK for smoking cessation are nicotine replacement therapy (NRT); the antidepressant Bupropion prolonged release tablets and Varenicline Tartrate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following unsafe practices of injecting opioid is associated with Candida endophthalmitis?

options.text: Injecting in the direction of blood flow

questions.explanation: Harm reduction advice for opiate users include not using opiates while alone; avoid use in combination with other drugs; avoid IV route; always inject in the direction of blood flow (in veins, this is towards heart); rotate injection sites; use new sterile needles and syringes on each occasion using sterile water - avoid lemon juice which can cause Candida endophthalmitis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the main side effect of varenicline?
questions.explanation: Varenicline Tartrate is a partial agonist binding with high affinity to alpha4beta2 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor. The main side effect is nausea (30%).

questions.question_text: Caffeine may elevate mood through increasing release of
questions.explanation: Caffeine may elevate mood through increasing release of noradrenaline (norepinephrine).

questions.question_text: Mrs. Z has a history of abusing illicit drugs. She became pregnant and has now given birth to a boy. He was fine for first 24 hours after birth. However, he is now irritable with frequent yawning, sneezing, loose stools, and fever. Tremors and jittery movements, along with high-pitched cry were observed. Which of the following drugs when used by mothers during pregnancy can present with these withdrawal symptoms in the neonates?
questions.explanation: Neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome usually begins 24-48 hours after birth, depending on the time of last dose.

questions.question_text: You are called to A and E to see a young American tourist having taken phencyclidine (PCP). Which of the following is least likely to be present?

options.text: Numbness or diminished responsiveness to pain

questions.explanation: Hallucinogen intoxication generally present with marked anxiety or depression, ideas of reference, fear of losing one's mind, paranoid ideation, and perceptual changes. Seizures are very rare.

questions.question_text: Which of the following can reduce the harm associated with injecting opioid?

options.text: Injecting in the direction of blood flow
Seeking out isolated and quiet places to inject
Injecting in the peritoneum to avoid clotting

correct_answer.text: Injecting in the direction of blood flow

correct_answers.text: Injecting in the direction of blood flow

questions.explanation: Using opiates while alone can increase the risk of overdose. To reduce harm, users are encouraged to avoid use in combination with other drugs; avoid IV route; always inject in the direction of blood flow (in veins, this is towards heart); rotate injection sites; use new sterile needles and syringes on each occasion using sterile water.

questions.question_text: Following smoking cessation, women and heavy smokers are at greatest risk for which of the following?
questions.explanation: Following smoking cessation, smokers report cravings for cigarettes, which can last for a longer period. The mean weight gain after smoking cessation is approximately 10 lb, and women and heavy smokers are at greatest risk for large weight gain.

questions.question_text: What percentage of those with alcohol withdrawal experience delirium tremens?
questions.explanation: In most severe cases of alcohol withdrawal syndrome, delirium tremens may develop - this includes 5% of all cases.

questions.question_text: In Wernicke's encephalopathy the classic triad of ataxia, confusion and ophthalmoplegia is seen in
questions.explanation: Wernicke's encephalopathy is an acute condition characterized by the well-known triad of 1. Ophthalmoplegia 2. Ataxia 3. Global confusional state. This classic triad of confusion, ataxia and nystagmus is only present in 10% of patients.

questions.question_text: The percentage of men in the UK who drink excessively, above the recommended weekly limits for sensible drinking, is
questions.explanation: 27% of men and 15% of women in the UK drink excessively, above the recommended weekly limits for sensible drinking ONS, 1998).

questions.question_text: What is the lifetime risk of suicide in dependent drinkers?
questions.explanation: Suicide risk is generally quoted as lifetime risk of 10 -15% in dependent drinkers.

questions.question_text: What is the minimum duration required to make a diagnosis of alcohol dependence according to ICD-10 criteria?
questions.explanation: ICD10 alcohol dependence requires at least 3 out of following list satisfied in last 12 months.

questions.question_text: Cerebellar degeneration has been reported to occur in about
questions.explanation: Degeneration of Purkinje cells in the cerebellar cortex (by 10-35 per cent) resulting in cerebellar atrophy has been reported to occur in about 40% of chronic alcoholics.

questions.question_text: Mr Z suffers from alcohol dependence syndrome of moderate severity. He is due to be started on chlordiazepoxide regime. The typical regime usually lasts for
questions.explanation: A typical regimen for alcohol dependence of moderate severity might be 10-20 mg QDS, reducing gradually over 5 -7 days.

questions.question_text: The starting dose of acamprosate in adults weighing 60 kg or more
questions.explanation: The starting dose of acamprosate in adults (18-65 year) weighing 60 kg or more is 666 mg three times daily.

questions.question_text: The symptoms of delirium tremens peak at
questions.explanation: The symptoms of delirium tremens peak between 72 and 96 hours after the last drink.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about relapse prevention in alcohol dependence?

options.text: Smoking is contraindicated when taking disulfiram
Acamprosate is not licensed for the elderly
If a patient relapses on acamprosate it must be stopped at once
Acamprosate and disulfiram must not be combined
Naltrexone has no place in treating alcohol dependence

correct_answer.text: Acamprosate is not licensed for the elderly

correct_answers.text: Acamprosate is not licensed for the elderly

questions.explanation: Acamprosate is not licensed for geriatric use.

questions.question_text: Which term refers to 'discrete episodes of anterograde amnesia that occur in association with alcohol intoxication'?
questions.explanation: Alcohol-related blackouts are not included in DSM5/ICD10. Blackouts are discrete episodes of anterograde amnesia that occur in association with alcohol intoxication.

questions.question_text: A 49-year-old man is heavily dependent on alcohol. Due to various physical problems, he was strongly advised to abstain. Unfortunately, since the last episode of intoxication he has developed recurrent voices that frighten him. In spite of 2 months of abstinence these hallucinations continue, and he now presents with persecutory delusions. Which of the following diagnosis best suits his presentation?
questions.explanation: The DSM-5 has a diagnostic criteria for substance-induced psychotic disorders (when induced by alcohol, this is popularly called alcoholic hallucinosis).

questions.question_text: Which of the following medication is better avoided for alcohol detoxification due to the risk of respiratory depression?
questions.explanation: Chlormethiazole can be used but better avoided for detoxification from alcohol as there is a higher risk of respiratory depression with its use in alcoholics.

questions.question_text: Choose the one feature that is not described under Edwards and Gross criteria (1976) for alcohol dependence
questions.explanation: Edwards and Gross criteria (1976) for alcohol dependence: 1. narrowed repertoire 2. salience of alcohol seeking behaviour 3. increased tolerance 4. repeated withdrawals 5. Drinking to prevent or relieve withdrawals.

questions.question_text: Characteristic features of delirium tremens include all except
questions.explanation: Features of alcohol withdrawal: Usually starts within 12 hours of last drink.

questions.question_text: Mr. Z was admitted to a medical ward for alcohol withdrawal syndrome and later he developed seizures. Which drug is most helpful in this situation?
questions.explanation: A meta-analysis of trials assessing efficacy of drugs preventing alcohol withdrawal seizures has demonstrated that benzodiazepines particularly long acting preparations such as Diazepam significantly reduces seizures de novo.

questions.question_text: Acamprosate appears to act centrally on which of the neurotransmitter systems?
questions.explanation: Acamprosate is a synthetic taurine analogue, which appears to act centrally on glutamate and GABA neurotransmitter systems.

questions.question_text: A 46-year-old gentleman has been started on disulfiram for the treatment of alcohol dependence. A common side effect reported by patients on taking disulfiram is
questions.explanation: Halitosis is a common side effect of Disulfiram.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medication used for delirium tremens may increase the risk of withdrawal seizures?
questions.explanation: Of all the above choices, only haloperidol lowers the seizure threshold.

questions.question_text: Patients with Wernicke's encephalopathy show gliosis and small haemorrhages especially in which of the following brain regions?
questions.explanation: Patients with Wernicke's encephalopathy show gliosis and small haemorrhages in periventricular and periaqueductal structures especially, the mamillary bodies.

questions.question_text: MATCH trial is a landmark study evaluating treatment options for alcohol dependence. Which of the following is an accurate finding from the MATCH trial?

options.text: At least initially drinkers with high psychiatric morbidity do better with CBT than 12 step programmes
Younger drinkers do better with a motivational approach
Matching patients to treatment options does not make a significant impact on outcome
Binge drinkers do better with a CBT approach
Impulsivity is the strongest predictor of long term drinking outcome

correct_answer.text: Matching patients to treatment options does not make a significant impact on outcome

correct_answers.text: Matching patients to treatment options does not make a significant impact on outcome

questions.explanation: There was little evidence for matching improving overall outcome.

questions.question_text: The two interventions compared in UK Alcohol Treatment Trial (UKATT) were

options.text: Motivational therapy vs. twelve step programme
CBT vs. social behaviour and network therapy
Motivational therapy vs. social behaviour and network therapy

correct_answer.text: Motivational therapy vs. social behaviour and network therapy

correct_answers.text: Motivational therapy vs. social behaviour and network therapy

questions.explanation: UKATT (United Kingdom Alcohol Treatment trial) compared Motivational Enhancement Therapy and Social Behaviour and Network Therapy in treating alcohol problems.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements concerning neuroimaging in Wernicke's encephalopathy is NOT true?

options.text: MRI is the most valuable diagnostic tool for Wernicke's
MRI cannot predict progression to Korsakoff's psychosis
MRI is better than CT scan for suspected Wernicke's
MRI may show mamillary body lesions
MRI has high sensitivity but poor specificity

correct_answer.text: MRI has high sensitivity but poor specificity

correct_answers.text: MRI has high sensitivity but poor specificity

questions.explanation: MRI has a sensitivity of only 53%, but its high specificity of 93% means that it can be used to confirm a suspected diagnosis.

questions.question_text: An opioid receptor antagonist that is effective in reducing craving for alcohol is
questions.explanation: Naltrexone is an opioid receptor antagonist used for the treatment of alcohol dependence.

questions.question_text: The symptom/sign that responds earlier than others when thiamine is replaced in a patient with Wernicke's encephalopathy is
questions.explanation: Ophthalmoplegia responds within hours, but cognitive impairment takes longer.

questions.question_text: Mr. Y was assessed by the drug and alcohol team and suggested alcohol detoxification. He is a chronic smoker and has a history of a chronic respiratory disease. Which one of the following is the most suitable drug for detoxification?
questions.explanation: Oxazepam is useful in patients with chronic respiratory disease.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an important adjunctive treatment for the prophylaxis and treatment of Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome?
questions.explanation: Parenteral vitamin replacement is an important adjunctive treatment for the prophylaxis and or treatment of Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome and other vitamin related neuropsychiatric conditions.
